author: GREG ISENBERG
text:
Someone will make $1B in the "digital detox" space. 

Tons of opportunity with the business thesis of: IRL > URL

2024 will be the turning point. People are realizing their phones are drugs. 

It's kinda like fast-food. 

The Big Mac you eat might have felt good in the moment, but the remorse creeps in as your stomach start turning.

Instant gratification of digital devices is turning into instant regret for millions.

So, selling "reset your mind and earn your freedom" will be compelling to many (and is to me).  More and more people want to detox.

The market could easily support many hundreds of $1M/year businesses. 

And I bet being more dopamine sober than dopamine drunk will be a modern day flex.

The internet used to be a place to get away from real life.

Now, real life is a place to get away from the internet.

--

topReplies.text: Greg, you’re are the modern days Nostradamus.

topReplies.author: Ian Storrar
topReplies.text: This is the future. Almost all my peers locally are looking for more IRL connection and community and use 2.0 technologies sparingly. It’s no surprise that we, the first generation on FB and Twitter, are now detoxing and resetting. Subscribing to your newsletter. Thanks!

topReplies.author: 𝒟𝑒𝓇𝑒𝓀
topReplies.text:
There’s something Matrix-esque about this. 

Something about how— only once he’s detached from its control, is he able to master and control the matrix itself. 

Makes you think…

topReplies.author: Jason Shuman
topReplies.text: Seeing a ton of pitches for micro format sauna, cold plunge, float tank and other alternative modality centers to help people unplug. The hole being created by declining religion rates in the U.S. is opening up many opportunities for mindfulness, community and routine.

topReplies.author: Sam
topReplies.text:
This narrative has been around for a while & on the surface I agree. 

I certainly share the sentiment.

However. 

The economic incentive of being here has too of high an opportunity cost to neglect.

Short-term detox is valuable; but like fasting… too much and you starve.
